clue.text: Cheers undead on the move around France, enjoying the victims' plight

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the single letter for France
letters on the move are shifting about, so the two words Cheers and undead are rearranged

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Zombies cheering as they roam round France, gleefully watching their victims suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' is the anagram signal and 'around' the container; the German word sits naturally in a scene of gloating undead.
explanation.definitionFit: The German loanword names pleasure taken in another person's misfortune, which is exactly relishing a victim's plight.

clue.text: Group of travellers are almost entering Irish county

indicators.note: entering means the shortened word goes inside the county name

parts.note: Cavan is a county in the Republic of Ireland

indicators.note: almost means the word are loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A band of travellers is nearly arriving in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cavan is a county in the Republic of Ireland; 'almost' and 'entering' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a company of travellers journeying together, as across a desert with camels.

clue.text: Gossip one had about broken leg is suggesting painkiller

indicators.note: had about means held around, so the gossip and one together enclose the other letters

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about someone, hence gossip
one is the indefinite article a

indicators.note: broken means the letters of leg and is are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Chat about someone's broken leg hints that they need pain relief.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of table talk, is a crossword favourite for gossip. 'broken' gives LGESI; 'suggesting' is a link, and analgesia is strictly the relief rather than the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is freedom from pain brought about by drugs, so it stands loosely for the relief a pain-relieving medicine gives.

clue.text: Specific duties mostly upheld after intervention by college

indicators.note: after intervention by means another piece has been put into the middle of the word
upheld in a down clue means the letters are turned to read upwards, i.e. backwards
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: duties levied by government are taxes

explanation.surface: Particular taxes, largely supported, once a college has stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upheld' means read upwards; with 'mostly' and 'after intervention by' that yields EXAT split by C.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and specific are synonyms, both meaning precise and particular rather than general.

clue.text: Supports love, taking men in affairs

indicators.note: in means the combined pieces are placed inside the word for affairs

parts.note: brief romantic affairs are flings

indicators.note: taking means the love letter takes the men along with it, sitting next to them

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, hence men

explanation.surface: Someone backs romance, bringing men into their love affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers; 'taking' and 'in' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Floorings are the boards and surfaces laid down underfoot, which support people and furniture above.

clue.text: Rising expectation about century being a significant period

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the letter for century
rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: hope is an expectation of something good
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence century

explanation.surface: Growing hopes over a hundred years mark an important era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads upwards in a down clue, giving EPOH, which 'about' wraps round C.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a notable era in history, one marked by some momentous event or change.

clue.text: Offer about routine practices taken up, producing upset

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means the whole assembly reads upwards, i.e. backwards
about means the offer goes around the routine practices

parts.note: an offer at auction is a bid
ruts are routines one gets stuck in

explanation.surface: A bid concerning established practices is raised, causing a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes BRUTSID, and 'taken up' reads it upwards in this down clue; 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to upset, unsettling someone's calm or the normal order of things.

clue.text: When moved I seek only to take in timeless liturgy in part of Mass

indicators.note: to take in means the rearranged letters enclose the shortened liturgy word
when moved means the letters of I seek only are shifted into a new order
timeless means the letter T, short for time, is removed

parts.note: a rite is a liturgical ceremony

explanation.surface: An emotional worshipper says they just want to absorb a timeless liturgy at Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' means losing T, the abbreviation for time; 'When moved' is the anagram signal and 'to take in' the container. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kyrie, Greek for 'Lord, have mercy', is an opening prayer and sung section of the Mass ordinary.

clue.text: Weatherproof clothing father used around sailing vessel

indicators.note: used around means the father's letters are wrapped around the vessel

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Noah's ark is the famous sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Dad wears a waterproof coat around the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used around' is the container signal; the ark is Noah's.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded, windproof and waterproof jacket, originally Inuit outerwear.

clue.text: Tough proposition, performing minus soprano

indicators.note: performing means the letters of minus soprano are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A singing show without its soprano is a hard task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' looks like part of the concert picture but signals the anagram of MINUS SOPRANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'bridge of asses', it names Euclid's fifth theorem, a stumbling block for beginners, hence any testing problem.

clue.text: Royal Sumo wrestling, with lots of clinches?

indicators.note: wrestling means the letters of Royal and Sumo grapple into a new order

explanation.surface: Imperial sumo bouts, full of grappling holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clinches' are wrestlers' holds in the surface but lovers' embraces in the definition; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting amorously, full of love, involves plenty of embracing, which is the other sense of clinches.

clue.text: One gives directions to a raving lunatic

indicators.note: lunatic means the letters of to a raving go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouts instructions at a ranting madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raving' and 'lunatic' both suggest madness; 'lunatic' is the anagram signal for TO A RAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, plane or rally car, the person who plots the route and tells the driver where to go is this crew member.

clue.text: Alluring woman helping to entrench our insecurities

indicators.note: helping to means the answer is a portion served up from within the words entrench our insecurities

explanation.surface: A seductress serves to deepen our self-doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition a houri is a beautiful maiden of paradise, so by extension any voluptuous, alluring woman.

clue.text: More than one relative hangs around after husband leaves

indicators.note: leaves means the husband letter departs from the word

parts.note: a ghost haunts a place, hanging around it

explanation.surface: A relative lingers once the husband has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops H from HAUNTS. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives, parents' sisters, and the plural matches 'More than one'.

clue.text: Painter studies board

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart, so cons are studies
a board can be a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: An artist examines a panel.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain and Suffolk scenes.

clue.text: Gallant expression of support incorporating a lot of sound

indicators.note: incorporating means the cheer takes the other letters into its body

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a sound argument is a valid one

explanation.surface: A dashing knight's cheer contains a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like noise but means valid, as in a sound argument; 'a lot of' and 'incorporating' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a knight or cavalier, and also a courtly, attentive man, so a gallant.

clue.text: Cover unusual rant about 8th-century pope

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the name of the pope
unusual means the letters of rant appear in an odd order

parts.note: Paul I was pope from 757 to 767

explanation.surface: A strange tirade concerning an early medieval pontiff is hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes TARN, which 'about' wraps round PAUL I, pope from 757 to 767.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet used to protect things from rain, a cover.

clue.text: Pagans — ideal sort for conversion

indicators.note: for conversion means the letters of ideal sort are changed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Heathens are the perfect people for a missionary to convert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' is a religious word in the surface, but here it changes the letters of IDEAL SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolaters worship idols or false gods, which is how monotheists have described pagans.

clue.text: Independent supporting article after writer interrupts old King out of doors

indicators.note: interrupts means the group of letters breaks into the old king pair

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: after means the writer comes before the next pair of letters
supporting in a down clue means sitting below the article and holding it up

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, hence writer
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An independent politician backs a piece after a journalist cuts into an old monarch's affairs, outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts I under A to give AI; 'after' sets AI after PEN; 'interrupts' pushes PENAI between O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air means taking place outdoors, outside rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Old magistrate always backtracking about end to crime

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the final letter of crime
backtracking means the word goes back the way it came, read backwards

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

indicators.note: end to means only the last letter of crime is used

explanation.surface: An old judge keeps retreating from his ruling about the end of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' reverses EVER to REVE, and 'about' puts it around E, the last letter of 'crime', after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English local official with magisterial powers, as in shire-reeve, the origin of sheriff.

clue.text: Area that's isolated — as a result, not initially having toilet installed

indicators.note: installed means the toilet is fitted inside the shortened word
not initially means the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: hence means as a result, therefore
lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: A remote area, so the first thing it lacked was a fitted toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' leaves ENCE and 'installed' is the container signal; LAV is British slang for a toilet. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory entirely surrounded by another, so cut off from its own country.

clue.text: Old theatre recalled a musical work

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the theatre word is read backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A former theatre remembered staging a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reads as remembered, but here it means called back, so the theatre word is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music and sung, a musical composition for the stage.

clue.text: A vital urge to abandon party, making excuse

indicators.note: to abandon means the party letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: libido is the life force or sexual drive, a vital urge
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A strong urge to skip the party, giving a reason not to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes DO from LIBIDO to give LIBI. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, and by extension any excuse.

clue.text: Everyone is devouring article linked to church marriages

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: devouring means the word is swallows the joined article and church letters
linked to means the article is joined directly onto the church abbreviation

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: All are eating an article tied to the church weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked to' joins the article and the church, and 'devouring' puts that pair inside the clue's own word 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliances are unions, and the word is used of marriages joining two families.

clue.text: Song higher in the charts in store

parts.note: a lay is a poem or ballad meant to be sung
a record higher in the charts is up

explanation.surface: A tune climbing the charts is on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in store' reads as coming soon, but 'in' is a link and 'store' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay up is to put away for future use, to stockpile or keep in reserve.

clue.text: International friendship apparently interrupted by rejection of popular agreement

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, an international body

indicators.note: interrupted by means another piece breaks into the middle of the phrase

parts.note: amity means friendship

indicators.note: rejection of means the word for popular is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Global goodwill seemingly broken when the popular agreement is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' gives NI and 'interrupted by' is the container signal; 'apparently' hints that the answer looks like a phrase about the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimity is complete agreement, everyone holding the same opinion.

clue.text: Succeed at school, with inclination to accept basic element of education

indicators.note: to accept means the lean takes in another letter

parts.note: a lean is a slope or tendency, an inclination
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of education, so R is one element

explanation.surface: Do well in class with an aptitude for the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic) are the basics of schooling; 'to accept' is the container signal and 'with' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to gain knowledge, which is what doing well as a pupil amounts to.

clue.text: Hawk heading off with energy, repeatedly circling swans, showing ulterior motive

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the hawk is removed

parts.note: a harrier is a bird of prey of the hawk family

indicators.note: circling means the energy letters go around the swans

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy, and repeatedly gives it more than once, here three times
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: A bird of prey takes off energetically, circling swans again and again with a hidden purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the first letter; 'repeatedly' here supplies three Es, which 'circling' places one before and two after the swans. Pens are female swans.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means a mental reservation or hidden intention, a thought kept behind the stated one.
